Strategy built on more than one point of view.

Sara Kim (김설아) — a strategy & operations consultant across Kearney, PwC, and Ewha Consulting ECON. Raised between Korean, English, and Mandarin, I've learned that the fastest way to see a structural problem is to look at it from a culture that doesn't share your assumptions.

Kearney PwC Ewha Consulting ECON Ewha Womans University · B.A. 2027
01 — About

I grew up comparing perspectives before I had a word for it. Nine years at international schools in Shanghai meant switching between Korean, English, and Mandarin before lunch, and treating a room full of different assumptions as the default, not the exception.

That instinct got formal training early. I started doing Model UN as a kid, arguing positions I didn't choose and defending interests that weren't mine — a strange way to build a worldview, but it worked: I got used to seeing an issue from outside whichever seat I happened to be sitting in.

Basketball taught me the other half. As a front guard for my university team now, the part I actually love isn't scoring — it's the four-person problem of reading teammates in real time and making the play work anyway.

Somewhere in that mix, in middle school, a former strategy consultant came to speak, and I remember thinking that getting paid to figure out why something was actually happening sounded like the best job in the world. I've been chasing that ever since.

It shows up in how I work now. Across engagements at Kearney and PwC, I've sat through 160+ expert and client interviews, joined executive workshops built for people twice my seniority, and made it my job to ask the question the room hadn't gotten to yet — a different market, a different supplier, a different set of assumptions — before accepting the version everyone else had already agreed on.

I like problems that don't have a shape yet, and I'd rather be the person asking an unfamiliar question than the person confirming a familiar one.

03 — Selected Projects

Case studies

Professional Experience
KEARNEY

Panel Sourcing, Root Cause

LCD Panel Supply Strategy
Challenge
Client's LCD panel sourcing depended on a single supplier type, but the structural reason behind that dependency hadn't been diagnosed.
Action
Traced the dependency to its root: IPS-only panel adoption excluded access to VA-panel suppliers under China's duopoly market. Recommended a VA-panel R&D and product design initiative to diversify sourcing.
Impact
Shaped client's mid-term panel sourcing strategy.
KEARNEY

Competitor Model Selection

Panel BOM Teardown
Challenge
Client needed a representative low-end competitor TV model for a panel BOM cost teardown, with no clear target defined.
Action
Independently screened TCL's full U.S. retail footprint — TCL.com, Best Buy, Walmart, The Brick — including discontinued SKUs, then validated the choice via sales-volume representativeness analysis (top 9 models ≈ 86–87% of category volume).
Impact
Delivered the benchmark-model recommendation that anchored the client's cost analysis.
KEARNEY

DRAM & the HBM Shift

Memory Sourcing Strategy
Challenge
Surging HBM/AI-server demand was reshaping DRAM supply-demand dynamics faster than client's existing sourcing models could track.
Action
Reverse-engineered ASP benchmarks across 6 global DRAM suppliers, modeled bit-growth vs. demand, and designed a methodology using crawled market-research data to estimate competitor cost-reduction targets.
Impact
Informed client's short- and mid/long-term memory sourcing strategy.

ECONPM

A GTM Path for Smart-Manufacturing Cloud

Client: NHN Cloud — Vertical GTM Strategy
Challenge
NHN Cloud needed a go-to-market path into smart manufacturing, but the roadmap had to hold up against how actual manufacturers and MES vendors operate — not just desk research.
Action
As PM, structured the analysis across four phases — sector trends, competitor analysis, self-assessment, positioning — segmenting the client base into four technology-tier packages, then engineered a dual-track roadmap around Composable MES and PMDC. Validated the roadmap through regular client meetings with NHN Cloud and an expert interview with Interx, an early-stage manufacturing-tech startup, to pressure-test feasibility before finalizing the recommendation.
Impact
Defined a white-space entry strategy for SME manufacturers, grounded in both the client's perspective and independent industry validation.

An IP Strategy for a Legacy Magazine Brand

Challenge

ECONMember

An Eco-Material Strategy for Home Appliances

Client: LG Chem
Challenge
LG Chem's eco-friendly material portfolio existed at the level of material science, but hadn't been translated into concrete component-level specifications for any actual product line.

ECONMember

Quantifying a Rental-Conversion Revenue Opportunity

Client: Coway — Subscriber Conversion Strategy
Challenge
Coway needed to identify and size the addressable market for converting bottled-water subscribers into water-purifier rental customers.
Action
Built TAM–SAM–SOM sizing from the ground up using data crawled across major retail channels (Naver, Kurly, Gmarket, Kakao) to estimate real subscription-service penetration, then estimated the break-even point (BEP) for the SOM-level segment the client should target first.
Impact
Identified and quantified a ≈KRW 196B revenue-generating market (SOM), giving the client a validated, BEP-tested segment to target.
